title: Port Ellis is a tourist trap
passage: Stopped in Port Ellis for one night on our road trip. The two restaurants we tried by the harbor were overpriced, and one waiter barely looked at us. The sunset from the pier was gorgeous, I'll give it that. But the whole town is clearly built to squeeze tourists. Save your money and keep driving.
cue: the whole town is clearly built to squeeze tourists
explanation: Marcus judges an entire town from one night and two harbor restaurants, which are the places most likely to cater to tourists. That's far too small and skewed a sample to describe the whole town.

whyNot.fal_anecdotal_evidence: Marcus isn't brushing aside any data with his story; he simply stretches a tiny sample into a verdict on the whole town.

passage:
Rachel: Our sitter from the Hatchsit app canceled an hour before date night. Again.
Ben: Ugh, sorry. That's the worst.
Rachel: That's both sitters we've booked through it, and both bailed. App sitters are just unreliable. I'm only asking the neighbors' teenagers from now on.
cue: both bailed. App sitters are just unreliable.
explanation: Rachel writes off every sitter on the app after two cancellations. Two people can't tell her much about the hundreds of sitters who use it.

whyNot.fal_anecdotal_evidence: Rachel isn't setting her experience against ratings or data; the flaw is generalizing from just two sitters.

title: Poll: our readers are done with flat phones
passage: In our weekend poll, 82% of the 3,400 readers who voted said their next phone will be a foldable. Folding screens have come a long way, with sturdier hinges and fewer creases than early models. With numbers like these, it's clear the mainstream market is ready to leave flat phones behind.
cue: it's clear the mainstream market is ready to leave flat phones behind
explanation: Circuit Weekly treats its own poll as a picture of the whole market. People who read a gadget site and vote in its polls are enthusiasts, not typical phone buyers, so 3,400 votes can't speak for the mainstream.

whyNot.fal_bandwagon: The poll isn't used to argue foldables are good because they're popular; it's used to predict the whole market from a skewed sample of fans.

source: Principal Dawn Achebe, Cedar Grove Elementary
title: Update on the new homework policy
passage: Dear families, thank you for your patience as we tried our new nightly reading log this month. I've now heard from three parents, and all three say their children feel overwhelmed. It's clear the policy isn't working for our families, so we'll pause it from Monday. Teachers will share a lighter plan next week.
cue: It's clear the policy isn't working for our families
explanation: Principal Achebe decides for the whole school based on three emails. Parents who write in are often the most unhappy ones, so three messages can't show how most families feel.

whyNot.fal_anecdotal_evidence: No survey or data is being overridden here; the problem is treating three self-selected emails as the voice of all families.

source: CEO Lauren Mbeki · Fernwood all-hands meeting
passage: Six weeks ago our design team, all eight of them, piloted a four-day week. Output held steady, deadlines were met and satisfaction scores jumped. I want to thank them for being our guinea pigs. Results like that tell us the four-day week will work across Fernwood, so support, sales and the warehouse will switch over in January.
cue: Results like that tell us the four-day week will work across Fernwood
explanation: Lauren extends one small team's pilot to the whole company. Eight designers with flexible project work may tell her little about support lines, sales targets or warehouse shifts.

whyNot.fal_composition: Composition assumes the parts' traits belong to the whole; here one unusual team is treated as a fair sample of very different teams.

passage: Big news! At our farmers' market stall on Saturday, 47 out of 50 tasters picked our new oat-milk vanilla over our classic dairy version. Even allowing for people being polite, that's a landslide. So starting next month, we're going fully dairy-free at the shop, because that's clearly what our customers want now.
cue: that's clearly what our customers want now
explanation: Scoop & Spoon assumes Saturday's market tasters speak for all its customers. A farmers' market crowd stopping for a free sample may differ a lot from the regulars who come in for dairy scoops.

whyNot.fal_anecdotal_evidence: This is an actual tally, not a personal story outweighing data; the trouble is that the 50 tasters may not represent the shop's customers.

title: Most residents back longer library hours, city survey finds
passage: The city mailed surveys to 2,400 randomly selected households across all 12 wards and received 1,650 responses. Of those, 68% supported extending weekday library hours to 9 p.m., with majorities in every ward. With a margin of error of about 2 points, staff told council most residents favor the change.
cue: 2,400 randomly selected households across all 12 wards
explanation: The survey drew a large random sample from every ward, and support was a majority everywhere. That's a sound basis for saying most residents favor longer hours.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: The sample is large, random and spread across the whole city, so generalizing to residents as a whole is justified.

passage:
Jae: That cable shipment from Quorvex came in. I pulled 5 cables at random from five different boxes and tested them.
Renee: And?
Jae: All 5 failed the charge test. If only a few in the shipment were bad, hitting five failures in a row would be really unlikely. I'm rejecting the whole lot and filing a return.
cue: If only a few in the shipment were bad, hitting five failures in a row would be really unlikely
explanation: Five is a small sample, but Jae picked at random from different boxes, and every one failed. If defects were rare, that result would be very unlikely, so concluding the shipment is badly flawed is reasonable.

whyNot.fal_hasty_generalization: The sample is small but random, and five out of five failures is too extreme to blame on chance, so rejecting the lot is justified.
